topic: Saturday at the football with my dad
brief: Britpop song sung in a London (non-rhotic) accent; rhymes only need to work in that accent.
title: Saturday Three O'Clock
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Dad would park the car outside the bakery on the corner,
pull his scarf up past his chin and say it's getting warmer,
we'd queue behind the stand with half the people that he saw,
and every week he'd tell me this would be the year for sure.

[Chorus]
Saturday, three o'clock,
singing louder than the rest,
Saturday, three o'clock,
me and Dad and all the rest.

[Verse 2]
We never won a thing, we nearly did in ninety-four,
he cried the way he never cried when Mum walked out the door,
now I bring my daughter and I tell her what I saw,
and every week I tell her this will be the year for sure.

[Chorus]
Saturday, three o'clock,
singing louder than the rest,
Saturday, three o'clock,
me and Dad and all the rest.
reason: corner/warmer, saw/sure/door rhyme in the London accent the brief names; on topic, natural English, singable.
